card.decision: Should the __main__ block catch ValueError and print a clean one-line message to stderr with a non-zero exit, instead of showing a traceback for usage mistakes?

experts.why: Users read 'Traceback' as a crash; the usage hint should be the first thing they see.
The non-goal wording against converting ValueError to an exit code may forbid exactly this change.

options.consequence: Clean usage messages for routine typos. main() still raises, so library callers and tests are unaffected. Needs a reading of the non-goal that allows handling in __main__.
options.label: Catch ValueError in __main__, print str(exc) to stderr, exit 2

card.why: Wrong argument count and blank text both raise ValueError, which currently escapes the __main__ block as a Python traceback. The usage hint is the last line of that traceback. The plan's non-goals include 'converting it to an exit code', which may or may not cover a handler in __main__ (the plan's own non-goal on sys.exit only permits exits in __main__). Three reviewers raised the same point (r1-1, r1-3, r1-5).
